prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identity of its active form, which established the incretin principle underlying treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity.

statement.case_for: I keep my round-1 configuration: a single B027 prize for Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange did not change the science, it only made the question sharper. The chair has asked whether we honour GLP-1 physiology and molecular identity or incretin-based therapy. I read the achievement as the former. Holst's incretin physiology, Mojsov's identification of the biologically active GLP-1(7-36)amide/(7-37) forms and Drucker's work on receptor action, proglucagon-derived biology and the route to therapy form one discovery chain that fixed what the target is. The drugs follow from that chain, and their value is confirmed by large independent randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal risk. Maturity is not in question. I also hold that the six identical configurations do not count as evidence on their own. What matters is that the case survived each member's stated reservation without the science being disputed. I do not want a second part: no other shortlisted achievement matches B027 on mechanism plus consequence, and any pairing would cost one of three names whose claims are tied to the same discovery.
statement.case_against: The credit list cannot be made clean with three seats. If the Committee decides the achievement is the therapy, Knudsen's engineering of liraglutide and semaglutide belongs in the third seat and my trio would be wrong. Mojsov's priority for the active peptide relative to Habener and other early contributors is not something I can settle from the supplied material, so I am relying on the supplied credit list and not on an audit. If that priority were shown to be weak, my case for the third seat would weaken, and I would then have no good alternative among the credited names but Knudsen. There is also a real risk that we are carried by the public prominence of semaglutide and tirzepatide, while cleaner older mechanisms (cGAS-STING, the unfolded protein response) wait. I accept that risk because the physiology reading is the one that rests on discovery, but it remains a judgement.

responses.point: The chair moved in round 1 from an opening trio with Knudsen to Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and discloses that this shift came from colleagues, so it should not be read as independent confirmation.
responses.response: I appreciate the disclosure, and I agree it means the identical trios carry less weight than the count suggests. For my part I held this trio from the start of round 1 and I am not counting the chair's move as support. The question you set is the right one and my answer is that the achievement is physiology and molecular identity. Analogue engineering is excellent pharmaceutical development, but it needs the identified active peptide and the defined receptor biology as its starting point. If the Committee instead chose the therapy reading, I would accept Knudsen in place of Mojsov, but then the citation would have to say so and the Habener question would press harder, because a therapy prize invites the early peptide claims too. Because the physiology reading is the one we converged on, I am keeping Mojsov and wording the citation so that it names the active form and not a drug.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius names B025 (CAR-T) as the strongest fallback if B027 attribution cannot be defended, describing it as a clean concept-to-cure chain with its own Eshhar problem, and she asks whether Mojsov's priority can be substantiated against Habener's group.
responses.response: On Mojsov versus Habener I have no evidence in the supplied materials that decides the matter, and I will not claim one. What I can say is that the shortlist's credit for B027 is built on the physiology, and a doubt over one peptide-characterisation claim does not remove Holst and Drucker, who carry the incretin effect and the receptor biology. So the doubt reduces the strength of one seat, not the prize. On B025 I agree it is the best-documented clinical record of the fallbacks, but I would rank it behind B020 and B043 if B027 fell, because the credited trio of June, Sadelain and Rosenberg describes three strands, and the earlier chimeric-receptor concept is outside the list. That is the same defect we accept less readily in B027. Efficacy is also still concentrated in haematological malignancies. I would reconsider the order if a two-name CAR-T credit could be defended.

responses.point: Perlmann argues that a single-achievement prize with a physiology-centred credit fits B027 better than adding a second part, because splitting would dilute the strongest case, while also keeping orexin (B004) and cGAS-STING (B020) as alternatives.
responses.response: I agree with the single-part conclusion and I now hold it more firmly than in round 1, when I called a pairing merely awkward. A second part would reduce the B027 names or reduce the other part to a share of a divided prize, and nothing else on the shortlist is strong enough to justify that price. On the alternatives we differ in emphasis. You prefer orexin as the disease-linked option. I would keep B020 ahead of B004, because the Chen and Barber credit is two names and the mechanism is settled, while orexin has the de Lecea and Kilduff versus Yanagisawa and Sakurai priority split and an autoimmune aetiology of human narcolepsy that is not fully resolved. I would not call B004 weak. It is a worthwhile later candidate, and I leave it out of my two alternatives only because of the credit problem.

responses.point: El-Manira ranks B020 low because therapeutic validation of STING agonists and inhibitors is still pending, calling it mechanism-rich and consequence-poor, and wants the Ishikawa, Sun and Wu claims and the Vance and Burdette cyclic dinucleotide precedent understood first.
responses.response: This is a fair criticism and it changed how I describe B020, though not my ranking of it as an alternative. I should not have implied in round 1 that mechanistic maturity and clinical maturity are the same thing. They are not, and no STING-directed drug has yet shown the patient benefit that B027 has. But the Committee's question is whether the discovery has been confirmed and has changed a field, and cGAS and cGAMP as the DNA-sensing step, with STING as the adaptor, have done that across antiviral defence, autoimmunity and tumour immunity. I accept your point about attribution: the Chen and Barber pairing is cleaner than most on the list but not free of the Ishikawa, Sun and Wu questions. That is why I offer B020 as an alternative for a year in which B027 is set aside, not as a second part this year. I think we agree that it is a later-year prize.

responses.point: Linnarsson would not place the unfolded protein response (B043) ahead of a candidate with durable patient benefit, judging its translational link as limited even though the Walter and Mori credit is clean.
responses.response: I accept that distinction and I think it is a real difference in how we weigh consequence, not in how we read the science. I keep B043 as my second alternative because its two-name credit is the cleanest on the shortlist and the IRE1, XBP1 and ER-to-nucleus signalling mechanism is textbook. I have to note again that IRE1-mediated splicing is close to my own RNA-processing interests, and I have tried not to let this raise the ranking. My argument for B043 is therefore its credit and maturity, not clinical benefit, and I agree it would not stand beside B027 on benefit. Where I would push back is only on treating limited disease consequence as a disqualifier for a physiology prize, since the UPR links to protein-misfolding and metabolic disease. I put it as the less consequential but better attributed of my two fallbacks.

uncertainties: Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1 peptide relative to Habener's group is unverified and cannot be settled from the supplied materials. If it were shown to be weak, the third seat would pass to Knudsen only under a therapy-centred citation.
Whether the Committee defines the achievement as GLP-1 physiology and molecular identity or as incretin-based therapy. I have assumed the first, and the wording of my citation depends on it.
Whether B020 or B043 is the better fallback. B020 has the greater breadth but its therapeutic validation is pending, and B043 has the cleaner credit but a more indirect disease link.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict with any shortlisted candidate or credited name. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson (eight recorded works, per my profile) and Jonas Frisen, and I work in the same single-cell genomics setting at Karolinska Institutet. None of them is a credited name on any shortlisted ballot. IRE1-mediated RNA splicing in B043 is close to my RNA-processing interests, but I have no documented tie to Walter or Mori, and I disclose this because B043 is one of my alternatives. No recusal is needed.
